question: Who among the following Indian reformers is credited with the campaign for widow remarriage and on whose suggestion a law was passed by the British officials in 1856, permitting the same?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar** **used the ancient texts to suggest that widows could remarry.**
 
• His suggestion was adopted by British officials, and a **law was passed in 1856 permitting widow remarriage.**
 
• Those who were against the remarriage of widows opposed Vidyasagar and even boycotted him.
 
• The Indian reformer credited with campaigning for widow remarriage and influencing the British officials to** pass a law permitting it in 1856 is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. **

 By the second half of the nineteenth century, the movement in favor of widow remarriage spread to other parts of the country.
 
• In Madras Presidency, **Veerasalingam Pantulu formed an association for widow remarriage.**
 
• Young intellectuals and reformers in Bombay pledged themselves to work for the same cause.
 
• In the north, **Swami Dayanand Saraswati also supported widow remarriage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
